To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a VLSI spiking network that can learn to classify linearly separable patterns of mean firing rate in an on-line and in a real-time manner, and (2) we show that this network is able to classify linearly non-separable patterns using an unsupervised learning rule.
we have proposed and implemented a VLSI architecture of spiking neurons that can be trained to classify complex spatiotemporal patterns in real time.
we have developed a compact, low-power VLSI network that can learn to classify patterns of mean firing rate in real-time, on-line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing biologically inspired VLSI architectures for learning and pattern recognition.
the development of a VLSI system that is able to learn to classify complex spatio-temporal patterns of mean firing rate on-line, in real-time and with very little hardware.
the study of the dynamics of networks of spiking neurons, the development of VLSI circuits that implement these networks, and the application of such networks to real-world problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed VLSI network has been shown to be capable of learning complex patterns of mean spike rates in a real-time, online fashion.
the proposed VLSI architecture can learn to classify spatial patterns of mean rates of spiking activity in real-time and with very little power consumption.

the network is able to learn to classify uncorrelated spatial patterns of mean rates, and that it is robust to noise in the input patterns, to the initial values of the synaptic weights, and to the initial conditions of the network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a VLSI system of spiking neurons can perform on-line supervised learning of complex patterns.
a VLSI implementation of the spiking neuron network is able to classify complex patterns with a high degree of robustness and reliability.
we have designed a VLSI circuit that can classify complex patterns of spiking activity in real-time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to implement an on-line, real-time, unsupervised learning mechanism using a network of spiking integrate-and-fire neurons connected by bistable plastic synapses.

a network of spiking integrate-and-fire neurons with bistable synapses can be used to learn to classify complex spatial patterns of mean activity on-line and in parallel, and that such learning can be performed using a simple local spike-based plastic mechanism.
the network is able to learn to classify complex input patterns in a compact and efficient way using a simple local plasticity mechanism.
